transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Greg. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Greg. Our upstairs S-Net WiFi booster is getting burning hot to the touch and the red warning light keeps flashing, causing our internet to drop every ten minutes. It is so hot that I burned my fingers when I picked it up, and I am terrified it is going to catch fire and burn down our house!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly investigate that overheating booster for you, Bethany. Before we check the hardware telemetry, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 72 Oakwood Avenue, Leeds, LS8 2PB. And my security question answer is my favourite primary school teacher, Mrs. Jenkins.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Bethany, that verifies your account file. What model is the WiFi booster unit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is the S-Net Smart WiFi Plus Disc, the white circular disc that pairs with the main Hub. My three-year-old daughter sleeps in the nursery right next to the booster, and with it burning this hot, I haven't slept a wink all night worrying about an electrical fire!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand your acute worry regarding the device temperature, Bethany, especially with your young daughter sleeping in the adjacent room. Electrical safety is our utmost priority, so let us immediately inspect the hardware logs and resolve the overheating safely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Greg, that reassures me immensely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your upstairs S-Net WiFi disc is overheating significantly, showing a flashing red thermal indicator and dropping connections, and you need the thermal hazard addressed immediately so your home remains safe and connected. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what we must sort out right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am querying the remote telemetry logs on your Smart WiFi Disc through our network management portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the temperature sensor report on the device?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The internal thermal sensor on the Broadcom radio chipset is reporting seventy-eight degrees Celsius, which automatically triggers safety thermal throttling.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Seventy-eight degrees! That is practically boiling point!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where is the WiFi booster physically positioned right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is sitting inside our wooden TV media console cabinet on the top shelf, right next to the games console and behind a decorative wicker basket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Enclosing the disc inside a wooden cabinet with games consoles traps thermal exhaust, preventing natural convection through the bottom ventilation louvers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I had no idea it needed so much airflow around it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Smart Disc uses passive convection cooling, requiring at least fifteen centimeters of open clearance on all sides.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me unplug it from the cabinet right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please unplug the power adapter from the mains wall socket, and allow the unit to rest on an open tabletop for ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugged it from the cabinet... moving it onto the wooden chest of drawers in the open landing hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Inspect the air vents on the underside of the base to verify they are free of domestic dust or pet hair.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Looking at the bottom... there is actually a thin layer of grey dust clinging to the circular intake grille.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Gently wipe the grille with a dry microfiber cloth or soft brush to clear the air passages.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wiping the vents with a soft duster... the plastic grille is completely clean and clear now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now inspect the black twelve-volt mains power adapter brick plugged into the wall outlet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking the power adapter brick... it is slightly warm, but completely normal, not hot at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the power supply regulation circuits are operating normally and delivering clean direct current.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's good. Now plugging the power lead back into the booster on the hallway chest of drawers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Allow two minutes for the mesh backhaul protocol to synchronize with the primary S-Net Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The LED light just changed from flashing amber to solid blue!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Solid blue indicates optimal mesh signal strength and normal operating temperature.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Touching the casing... it feels cool to the touch now, just mildly lukewarm instead of burning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am refreshing the hardware thermal telemetry on our monitoring dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the sensor show now on your screen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The chipset temperature has dropped from seventy-eight degrees to forty-two degrees Celsius, well below the sixty-five degree throttling threshold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is thirty-six degrees cooler! What a relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the position of your downstairs primary Hub to ensure it is not suffering similar ventilation restriction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The downstairs hub is on an open wooden telephone table in the hallway, completely out in the open with nothing covering it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Downstairs hub telemetry reports thirty-eight degrees Celsius, which is optimal ambient operating temperature.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, at least the downstairs unit is completely fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us check the mesh signal link quality between the downstairs hub and your newly repositioned upstairs disc.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we verify the wireless link speed between the two units?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The 5GHz dedicated wireless backhaul registers a negotiated link speed of six hundred and fifty megabits with negative fifty-five decibel signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like a very strong connection between floors.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Negative fifty-five decibels indicates excellent line-of-sight signal through the hallway stairwell.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test my laptop in the upstairs nursery right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead, let us verify wireless throughput and packet stability across the upstairs zone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening high-definition video stream on the laptop... playing smoothly at 1080p with zero buffering!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms thermal equilibrium has been restored by unrestricted convective airflow, Bethany.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The disc telemetry records zero dropped packets over the last three minutes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The wireless interface has transmitted over four gigabytes of test payload without a single retry.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we also turn down the bright blue front LED indicator at night so it doesn't disturb my daughter's sleep in the next room?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the S-Net mobile app under Booster Settings, enable 'Night Mode Dimming' to dim the LED indicator by ninety percent between nine in the evening and seven in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Enabling Night Mode Dimming now... the bright blue glare dropped to a faint glow immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What if it starts overheating again when the weather gets warmer in summer?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hardware thermal failures are strictly between you and the equipment manufacturer; S-Net does not insure or guarantee device temperatures against domestic room conditions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, S-Net supplied this booster as part of our monthly broadband contract! How can you say S-Net has no responsibility if your equipment overheats?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our terms of service cover broadband signal delivery, not ambient environmental temperature variations within your residence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like a complete brush-off. If a device supplied by you gets dangerously hot, S-Net should replace it immediately rather than blaming my room!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The unit is currently reporting forty-two degrees, which is normal factory specification.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It might be 42 degrees now on an open hallway table, but I am still very frightened that the internal electronics are faulty from running at 78 degrees all week!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Modern semiconductor chips possess integrated thermal protection circuitry that prevents silicon damage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least dispatch a replacement booster so I know my baby's bedroom is 100% safe?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Replacement hardware cannot be authorized when telemetry diagnostics report passing operational status.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So if the unit overheats again and melts while we are out, that's just our problem?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The device contains self-resetting thermal fuses that physically cut power in extreme fault conditions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thermal fuses don't give me peace of mind when my toddler is sleeping in the next room!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All S-Net telecommunications equipment complies with British Standard and CE electrical safety certifications.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, certifications or not, I am still terrified this unit is a fire hazard, and I do not consider this issue resolved or safe for my family!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The telemetry confirms normal function. Keep the vents clear and have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
